content: The designations and presentation of material in this publication do not reflect any opinion by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) or the World Health Organization (WHO) regarding the legal status of any country, territory, city, or area, or their authorities, nor do they address the delimitation of boundaries. Dotted lines on maps represent approximate borderlines where full agreement may not yet exist. The mention of specific companies or products, whether patented or not, does not imply endorsement or recommendation by FAO or WHO over others of a similar nature that are not mentioned. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters, and all reasonable precautions have been taken by FAO and WHO to verify the information in this publication. However, the material is distributed without any warranty, expressed or implied. The responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader, and FAO and WHO are not liable for any damages arising from its use. The views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily represent those of FAO or WHO. FAO and WHO encourage the use, reproduction, and dissemination of the material in this publication. FAO and WHO specifications are developed to promote, as far as practicable, the manufacture, distribution, and use of pesticides that meet basic quality requirements. Compliance with these specifications does not constitute an endorsement or warranty of a pesticide’s fitness for a particular purpose, including its suitability for controlling specific pests or its use in a particular area. The suitability of pesticides for specific purposes and the content of labeling instructions must be determined at the national or provincial level. Pesticides manufactured to comply with these specifications are not exempt from safety regulations or other legal provisions applicable to their manufacture, sale, transportation, storage, handling, preparation, or use. FAO and WHO disclaim liability for any injury, death, loss, or damage arising from the manufacture, sale, transportation, storage, handling, preparation, or use of pesticides claimed to comply with these specifications. Improper storage, handling, preparation, or use of pesticides can result in reduced safety or efficacy. FAO and WHO are not responsible for testing pesticides for compliance with specifications or for any methods recommended or used for such testing. Consequently, FAO and WHO do not warrant or represent that any pesticide claimed to comply with their specifications actually does so. FAO and WHO respect and safeguard confidential proprietary data provided for evaluation purposes. Such data will not be published or disclosed to third parties without authorization. Experts participating in evaluations are required to sign confidentiality agreements and are instructed not to share or use the data for purposes other than evaluation. Electronic transmission of confidential information is discouraged due to security concerns, and paper copies or encrypted optical storage media are recommended. After evaluations, all data are returned to FAO or WHO and kept secure, or destroyed if no longer needed. These specifications are developed through a transparent evaluation process involving the FAO/WHO Joint Meeting on Pesticide Specifications (JMPS). Specifications apply only to products from manufacturers whose data have been evaluated and found satisfactory by the JMPS. The process includes extensive consultation with stakeholders, and the resulting specifications are published online for transparency and accessibility. The FAO and WHO have a long history of collaboration in developing pesticide specifications. The FAO began this work in 1963, and the WHO established its Pesticide Evaluation Scheme (WHOPES) in 1960. Both organizations aim to promote the safe and effective use of pesticides while ensuring their quality. In 2001, FAO and WHO signed a Memorandum of Understanding to harmonize their specifications development processes. This collaboration led to the establishment of the JMPS, which held its first full meeting in 2002. The JMPS develops joint specifications for pesticides used in both agriculture and public health, ensuring consistency and reliability. The FAO/WHO Manual on Pesticide Specifications has undergone several revisions to reflect scientific and technological advancements. The most recent revision, published in 2016, incorporates updates and clarifications based on feedback from JMPS meetings and other stakeholders. The manual is available online and serves as the current working version for FAO and WHO purposes. The term pesticide encompasses active ingredients in any form, whether formulated for application or not. FAO and WHO specifications apply only to products from manufacturers whose technical materials have been evaluated and approved by the JMPS.
